SAS PRXMATCH(regular-expression-id | perl-regular-expression, source)

Source: R/doc_functions.R
sas_f_prxmatch.Rd

Position of the first match of a Perl regular expression. See the SAS documentation (Functions and CALL Routines).

Arguments

re

Pattern identifier returned by PRXPARSE, or a Perl regular expression string in delimiters (e.g. '/b+/').

x

Character source string to search; the result is the position of the first match, or 0.

.at

Internal: source position c(line, column) used in log NOTEs.

session

A session from sas_session() that holds the PRXPARSE ids, for calls outside sas_run() (inside a run, the running session is used).

Value

A vector with one result per element (arguments are recycled), as the SAS function returns per observation.

Differences from R

Implements the SAS DATA step semantics (log NOTEs, _ERROR_), which base R has no counterpart for.

See also

Other special functions: sas_f_band(), sas_f_blshift(), sas_f_bnot(), sas_f_bor(), sas_f_brshift(), sas_f_bxor(), sas_f_exist(), sas_f_input(), sas_f_inputc(), sas_f_inputn(), sas_f_missing(), sas_f_nvalid(), sas_f_prxchange(), sas_f_prxparse(), sas_f_put(), sas_f_putc(), sas_f_putn()

Examples

# PRXMATCH: each call is explained above it and followed by its result

# PRXMATCH returns the position of the first match of the Perl regular
# expression /b+/: 2.
sas_f_prxmatch("/b+/", "abbc")  # prxmatch('/b+/', 'abbc') = 2
#> [1] 2

# There is no match, so the result is 0.
sas_f_prxmatch("/z/", "abc")  # prxmatch('/z/', 'abc') = 0
#> [1] 0

# The i option makes matching case-insensitive, so /B/i matches 'b' at position
# 2.
sas_f_prxmatch("/B/i", "abc")  # prxmatch('/B/i', 'abc') = 2
#> [1] 2

# ^ anchors the match at the start, and the string starts with a blank, so
# there is no match.
sas_f_prxmatch("/^a/", " abc")  # prxmatch('/^a/', ' abc') = 0
#> [1] 0
